title: POC Weekly Sync - Quantization Experiments
summary: Weekly POC sync to review INT8/FP8 quantization results, quality delta analysis, and perf benchmarks. Team agrees INT8 gives best cost/throughput gains with minor quality impact on specific prompt families; FP8 shows additional perf but has stability/regression risks on longer contexts. Next steps: run expanded eval, 24h stability tests on FP8, tune per-layer ranges and batching configs, and share quant configs and scripts.
topics: Next steps for pilot and rollouts

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Avery Lin (Redwood AE), Marcus Reed (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (Acme ML Lead), Sam Ortega (Acme SRE), Priya Kumar (Acme Product)

Summary (auto): weekly POC sync to review quantization experiments (INT8/FP8), discuss quality impact, perf deltas, and next steps. Some transcripts sections contain minor mis-hearings; see action items for concrete owners.

[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we've got about 45 minutes today. The plan is quick results review, Marcus will walk through the numbers, then we discuss regressions you flagged and action items.
[00:32] Nina: Thanks, Avery. Quick note, Sam and I uploaded the latest production prompts — about 250 seeding prompts — and Priya will add business CR examples after.
[01:05] Marcus: Cool. I'll kick off with the INT8 vs FP8 summary then show the perf deltas on Dedicated testbed. Apologies in advance, some of the kernel names in the logs got munged — you might see "Redwood Dedic8" in places.
[02:10] Marcus: So baseline: FP16 on our dedicated node gives median latency 120ms for seq len 256, throughput ~600 tokens/sec, and cost X. With INT8 quant we saw roughly 1.7x throughput improvement and median latency down to about 85ms. With FP8 we saw up to 2.1x throughput improvement and latency ~60-70ms on short sequences.
[03:05] Priya: That's promising. What about quality — any measurable regressions? We care about hallucinations on clinical question prompts.
[03:40] Marcus: Right. We ran automated eval on 250 prompts with a mix: clinical Q/A, summarization, and policy detection. Metrics: exact-match-ish, and a manual spot-check for hallucination. INT8: average quality delta was small, like <1.5% in the task metric; most regressions were on a specific subset of instruction-style prompts. FP8: more variance — some prompts ok, but a few longer-context summarizations showed degraded coherence.
[04:50] Nina: Can you give an example of the prompt family where INT8 regressed?
[05:12] Marcus: Yep. It's mainly prompts with multi-step reasoning and long numerical contexts — e.g., "Given the following timeline of events, identify inconsistencies and produce a consolidated timeline." For those, INT8 sometimes dropped a step or re-ordered items. We saw about 6% failure rate on that bucket vs 1% baseline.
[06:05] Nina: Hmm that could be material. Were these reproducible?
[06:22] Marcus: Mostly yes, but there's some non-determinism. We suspect range estimation during static quantization missed some outlier activations in a few layers. We'll try per-layer calibration and potentially block-wise INT8.
[07:00] Sam: Did you use post-training static quant or dynamic quant? Also how was KV cache handled?
[07:18] Marcus: Good call. This run used post-training static quant with 256 calibration samples. KV cache was preserved and we did cache-aware batching — but sometimes FP8 runs hit OOM on longer sequences, which caused falls back to FP16 for those requests in the run. The FP8 memory improvements let us increase batch sizes, but stability is the trade-off.
[08:10] Priya: You mentioned OOMs — did that lead to failed responses or degraded quality?
[08:36] Marcus: For the FP8 smoke, OOMs led to process restarts on the test node in two of ten runs. Those specific requests either failed or were re-routed to baseline model, so quality wasn't evaluated consistently across those samples. That's why we want a 24h stability test.
[09:30] Nina: From a product perspective, if INT8 has small regressions only on narrow prompt families, we can probably proceed with a canary, but we need to know failure modes.
[10:05] Marcus: Agreed. We can instrument more logging: per-layer range histograms, activation max trace, and a per-prompt diff report (old vs quantized) that flags token-level divergences. We'll include that in the runbook.
[11:00] Avery: Can you also share the quant config and the script so Nina's team can reproduce exactly?
[11:12] Marcus: Yep, I'll push the quant config + runbook to the shared folder by Thursday (2025-02-13).
[12:00] Sam: On the infra side, we need a Dedicated test pool for the FP8 24h run. I'll raise the access ticket but need info on network rules and any special drivers.
[12:30] Marcus: The FP8 runs used an experimental driver and a specific kernel shim; I'll list the driver version and required CUDA/cuDNN stacks in the runbook.
[13:10] Priya: About metrics — can we get a simpler business-focused KPI? For us it's hallucination rate on clinical Qs and end-user latency p95.
[13:40] Marcus: We'll produce a small KPI dashboard: p50/p95 latency by seq len, hallucination count on labeled set, and token throughput. We'll also output cost delta estimates using Redwood pricing assumptions.
[14:30] Nina: You mentioned cost. Roughly what's the expected unit cost reduction with INT8 vs FP16?
[14:50] Marcus: Ballpark, INT8 reduces per-token GPU cost ~30-40% given throughput gains; FP8 could push to ~50% but with risk and engineering overhead. Those are estimates — we'll produce a cost table for your workload once you run the 500-prompt eval.
[16:00] Priya: For compliance, any change to logs or telemetry with quantized runs? We need audit traces for model version & quant config.
[16:22] Marcus: We tag each run with model hash + quant config id and include those tags in logs. We'll also export a small manifest of artifacts (config, calibration data sample ids) for audit. That should satisfy your SOC2 traceability ask.
[17:05] Sam: Ok, networking — when we do the canary on Dedicated, access will be from our VPC. Any special routing?
[17:25] Avery: Redwood Private can run in your VPC; for Dedicated we can do a private peering. Marcus, please include required firewall ports in the ticket.
[18:00] Marcus: Will do.
[18:45] Nina: Quick question — any mention of competitors performance? We briefly tried a bench of ModelCo's INT8 wrapper last month and results were inconsistent.
[19:05] Marcus: We saw similar patterns from ModelCo: INT8 often safe for short instructions, more fragile on multi-step. BigCloud AI had a managed FP8 offering but with limited context length. We're not assuming parity, just giving you the vendor context.
[20:00] Priya: For the canary strategy, what's the recommended rollout? 10% traffic for 48 hours?
[20:25] Marcus: We recommend starting with a small internal-only traffic slice (5-10%) on non-critical routes for 48 hours, monitor KPI delta threshold (e.g., hallucination delta <1%, p95 latency improvement >=15%), then expand to 50% and run a second smoke. If stable, do full switch or keep as fallback policy.
[21:30] Nina: That sounds fine. On the evaluation side, we'll add clinical long-form summarization and a few adversarial prompts.
[22:05] Marcus: Great. A couple notes from the logs: a few tokens were transcribed in the logs oddly — you may see "kv cash" instead of "KV cache" in some automated filenames. Ignore those; it's a transcription artifact.
[23:00] Avery: Ok let's summarize action items. Marcus will share quant configs and runbook by 2/13; Marcus to run 24h FP8 stability test by 2/18; Nina to upload 500-eval set by 2/20; Sam to create Dedicated access ticket by 2/14. Any additions?
[23:35] Priya: Please also share the per-prompt diff reports and the list of prompts that regressed.
[23:50] Marcus: Will include that in the zipped artifact.
[24:30] Avery: Great. We'll reconvene same time next week. Thanks everyone.

End transcript.
